Algorithm 1 RadioTrace

Input: Sparse RSS $O$, mask $\mathcal{M}$, building map $B$, $\#Tx$
$R$, diffusion model $f_\theta$, steps $T$, step size $\eta$, momentum $\beta$, anchor cap $\kappa$, Gaussian width $\sigma$, PG-KMeans iters $L_{\max}$, tol $\tau$

Output: Clean radio map $\mathbf{x}_0$, Tx coordinates $\Omega_0$

1: PG-KMeans init.: $\mathcal{S} \leftarrow \{(m_k, n_k) \mid \mathcal{M}=1\}$
2: Map RSS to ranges: $d_k \leftarrow \psi(\mathbf{O}(m_k, n_k))$
3: Init seeds $\{\omega_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^R$ uniformly on grid
4: for $\ell=0$ to $L_{\max}-1$ do
5:     Assign $k$ to $i=\arg\min_i$ $\left\|s_k-\omega_i^{(\ell)}\right\|-d_k$
6:     Back-project: $\tilde{\mathbf{\omega}}_k,i \leftarrow s_k+d_k\frac{\mathbf{\omega}_i^{(\ell)}-s_k}{\max\{\|\mathbf{\omega}_i^{(\ell)}-s_k\|,\varepsilon\}}$
7:     Update: $\mathbf{\omega}_i^{(\ell+1)} \leftarrow \frac{\sum_{k\in\mathcal{E}_i}\tilde{\mathbf{\omega}}_k\mathbf{\tilde{\omega}}_k}{\sum_{k\in\mathcal{E}_i}\mathcal{O}_k}$
8:     if $\max_i\|\mathbf{\omega}_i^{(\ell+1)}-\mathbf{\omega}_i^{(\ell)}\|\leq\tau$ then break
9: end for
10: $\Omega_T\leftarrow\{\mathbf{\omega}_i^{(\ell_{\text{end}})}\}_{i=1}^R$; sample $\mathbf{x}_T\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I})$
11: Set anchor $\Omega_T^*\leftarrow\Omega_T$; best loss $\mathcal{L}^*\leftarrow+\infty$
12: Initialize momentum $v_{a,i}=v_{b,i}=0$ for $i=1:R$
13: for $t=T$ to 1 do
14:     Build binary Tx map $\mathcal{C}_t$ with $\Omega_t$
15:     Predict noise: $\epsilon_\theta\leftarrow f_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t,t,\mathbf{B},\mathbf{C}_t)$
16:     $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_t^0\leftarrow\frac{1}{\sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_t}}\big(\mathbf{x}_t-\sqrt{1-\bar{\alpha}_t}\epsilon_\theta\big)$
17:     Sample $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$ with DDPM mean and variance
18:     $\kappa_t\leftarrow\kappa\cdot\frac{T-t}{T}$
19:     Loss: $\mathcal{L}_t\leftarrow\|\hat{\mathbf{x}}_0^t\odot\mathcal{M}\}-\mathbf{O}\|_{F}^2+\frac{\kappa_t}{2}\left\|\Omega_t-\Omega_t^*\right\|_{2}^2$
20:     Backprop to get $\nabla_{\Omega_t}\mathcal{L}_t$
21:     Update the coordinates to get $\Omega_{t-1}$
22:     if $\mathcal{L}_t<\mathcal{L}^*$ then $\mathcal{L}^*\leftarrow\mathcal{L}_t$, $\Omega_{t-1}^*\leftarrow\Omega_t$
23: end for
24: return $\mathbf{x}_0$, $\Omega_0$

We stop when  $ \max_i \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_i^{(\ell+1)} - \boldsymbol{\omega}_i^{(\ell)}\|_2 \leq \tau $ or when  $ \ell $ matches the max iterations  $ L_{\max} $. This propagation-guided K-means decreases (13) in practice and typically converges within 10 iterations by our numerical experience. Larger RSS indicates stronger links and typically shorter ranges, so weighting by  $ \tilde{O}_k $ prioritizes more informative samples while keeping the mechanics simple.
Putting all pieces together, the complete RadioTrace procedure is summarized in Algorithm 1.

This section analyzes the stability of the Tx-coordinate refinement component in the proposed RadioTrace framework. Due to the tightly coupled in-loop inference procedure, the effective refinement objective evolves across diffusion time steps, since the RM estimate and the relaxed Tx-map representation are progressively updated during reverse generation. We therefore formulate the Tx-coordinate update as a time-varying stochastic optimization process and analyze its long-term behavior under standard regularity conditions.

For the purpose of convergence analysis, we study the algorithm in the forward direction with time index  $ k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots $ instead of the diffusion reverse iteration, and rewrite the coordinate-refinement recursion accordingly. This re-indexing does not alter the algorithm but simplifies the subsequent analysis. At analysis step  $ k $, the reverse diffusion process produces a random RM reconstruction, which induces a stochastic loss function  $ L_k(\Omega; \xi_k) $, where  $ \Omega \in \mathbb{R}^{2R} $ denotes the Tx-coordinate vector and  $ \xi_k $ is a random variable, arising from the diffusion sampling and the rounding procedures.
